canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_1=(Λ,A,B,C,|Ψ^Λ⟩,\mathcal U,\mathcal M_B,Z_{\mathrm{SAW}},F_{\mathrm{SAW}},κ,L_x,L_y,Π_1)∈\mathcal O_P^{(1)}, where Π_1 is a proof certificate whose terminal judgement is an inequality for the average post-measurement entanglement entropy between A and C
canonical_goal.target_object: A proved proposition with endpoint: for a finite planar two-dimensional lattice Λ partitioned into measured region B and unmeasured regions A,C, local measurement of B produces conditional states |ϕ^{AC}_{s_B}⟩ whose average entropy E(A:C)=∑_{s_B}p_{s_B}S(ρ^A_{s_B}) is bounded below by 2F_{\mathrm{SAW}}-2log(eF_{\mathrm{SAW}}) whenever F_{\mathrm{SAW}}≥2; and, for explicitly specified random constant-depth two-dimensional circuit or holographic tensor-network ensembles with system-size-independent local dimension and depth, the ensemble average obeys \mathbb E_{U∼\mathcal U}∑_{s_B}p_{s_B}S(ρ^A_{s_B})≥κL_x for some κ>0 and all L_x above a finite constant.
feasibility_constraints: Λ=(V,E) is a finite planar graph embedded as a two-dimensional lattice with linear dimensions L_x,L_y; A,B,C⊆V are disjoint; measurements are performed only on B; a dual-lattice path W separates A from C iff every path in Λ from A to C crosses W.
The pre-measurement state is |Ψ^{ABC}⟩. For each local-basis outcome s_B on B, p_{s_B}=⟨s_B|ρ^B|s_B⟩ with ρ^B=Tr_{AC}[|Ψ^{ABC}⟩⟨Ψ^{ABC}|], and |ϕ^{AC}_{s_B}⟩=p_{s_B}^{-1/2}(⟨s_B|⊗I_{AC})|Ψ^{ABC}⟩.
The entropy to be bounded is E(A:C)=∑_{s_B}p_{s_B}S(ρ^A_{s_B}), where ρ^A_{s_B}=Tr_C[|ϕ^{AC}_{s_B}⟩⟨ϕ^{AC}_{s_B}|] and S(σ)=-Tr[σlogσ].

The general bound assumes strict locality: for every tripartition X∪Y∪Z=Λ such that no edge connects X to Z after removing Y, Tr_Y[ρ^{XYZ}]=ρ^X⊗ρ^Z. The tensor-network representation is isometric: the directed graph has no directed cycles and every local tensor is an isometry from its incoming virtual legs to all outgoing virtual legs together with its physical leg.

The general measurement condition is a local complex-projective 2-design POVM: at each measured site i with Hilbert-space dimension d_i, the POVM \mathcal M_i={F_{r_i}} satisfies ∑_{r_i}Tr(F_{r_i})(F_{r_i}/Tr(F_{r_i}))^{⊗2}=(I_i+\mathsf F_i)/(d_i+1), where \mathsf F_i swaps the two replicas of the site Hilbert space; the joint measurement is \mathcal M_B=⊗_{i∈B}\mathcal M_i.

For a separating dual self-avoiding walk W, let W^- be the set of sites directly adjacent to W on the A side and W^+ the set directly adjacent to W on the C side; define S_W^{(2)}=-logTr[(σ_r^{AW^-})^2], where σ_r^{AW^-} is the reduced state on AW^- after measuring the free A-side sites and conditioning on the outcome r. Strict locality implies S_W^{(2)} is independent of r and equals the Rényi-2 entropy of the complementary reduced state on W^+F_CC.

The self-avoiding-walk partition function is Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}=∑_{W∈\mathrm{SAW}(Λ^*,A,C)}exp[-H(W)] with H(W)=S_W^{(2)}/2; \mathrm{SAW}(Λ^*,A,C) is the set of self-avoiding walks on the dual graph Λ^* that separate A from C; F_{\mathrm{SAW}}=-logZ_{\mathrm{SAW}}.

For constant-depth circuit instantiations, |Ψ^Λ⟩=U|0⟩^{⊗N}, N=|V|, U is sampled from the ensemble named in the claimed subfamily, the circuit depth d_C is bounded by a constant independent of N, and the qudit dimension q is bounded by a constant independent of N.

Whenever a gate or on-site unitary is called Haar-random, its distribution is the unique probability measure on the corresponding finite-dimensional unitary group that is invariant under left and right multiplication by fixed unitaries.

success_set.definition: Σ_P^{(1)}={o_1: Π_1 proves all of the following self-contained statements. (a) General bound: if |Ψ^Λ⟩ satisfies strict locality and the local 2-design POVM condition, and if F_{\mathrm{SAW}}=-log∑_{W∈\mathrm{SAW}(Λ^*,A,C)}exp[-S_W^{(2)}/2]≥2, then ∑_{s_B}p_{s_B}S(ρ^A_{s_B})≥2F_{\mathrm{SAW}}-2log(eF_{\mathrm{SAW}}). (b) Holographic instantiation: if each edge e of Λ carries the same bipartite bond state |ω_e⟩ with S_e^{(2)}=-logTr[(Tr_2|ω_e⟩⟨ω_e|)^2], each bulk site is acted on by an independent Haar-random unitary, meaning a unitary drawn from the left- and right-invariant probability measure on the relevant finite-dimensional unitary group, and then measured, L_y is bounded above by a polynomial in L_x, and S_e^{(2)}>2logμ_{Λ^*} with μ_{Λ^*}=lim_{n→∞}c_n^{1/n} and c_n the number of length-n self-avoiding walks from a fixed dual vertex, then \mathbb E_U∑_{s_B}p_{s_B}S(ρ^A_{s_B})≥κL_x for all sufficiently large L_x and for every κ strictly smaller than S_e^{(2)}-2logμ_{Λ^*}. (c) Depth-2 4-local plaquette instantiation: for Haar-random, meaning invariant under left and right multiplication by fixed unitaries, four-qudit plaquette gates on the square-lattice architecture, with q∈\mathbb Z and q≥88, measuring B yields \mathbb E_U∑_{s_B}p_{s_B}S(ρ^A_{s_B})≥κL_x for some κ>0 and all sufficiently large L_x. (d) Depth-4 brickwork instantiation: for Haar-random, meaning invariant under left and right multiplication by fixed unitaries, two-qudit brickwork gates, with q∈\mathbb Z and q≥134, measuring B yields \mathbb E_U∑_{s_B}p_{s_B}S(ρ^A_{s_B})≥κL_x for some κ>0 and all sufficiently large L_x.}

robustness_scope.ambient_space: Tuples (Λ,L_x,L_y,A,B,C,\mathcal U,q,d_C,\mathcal M_B) satisfying the feasibility constraints for post-measurement entropy, where \mathcal U is one of the claimed random circuit or holographic tensor-network ensembles, q is a positive integer independent of N=L_xL_y, and d_C is a positive integer independent of N.
robustness_scope.indexing_set: {(Λ,S_e^{(2)},L_x,L_y): L_y≤L_x^a for some fixed a>0 and S_e^{(2)}>2logμ_{Λ^*}} ∪ {(q,L_x,L_y): q∈\mathbb Z, q≥88, depth-2 Haar-random 4-local plaquette gates} ∪ {(q,L_x,L_y): q∈\mathbb Z, q≥134, depth-4 Haar-random 2-local brickwork gates}

claimed_subfamily.definition: The claimed subfamily is exactly the union of three families. Family H: place a bipartite state |ω_e⟩ on every edge e, apply independent Haar-random (left- and right-unitarily invariant) unitaries to bulk sites, and measure bulk sites; for W∈\mathrm{SAW}(Λ^*,A,C), H(W)=S_e^{(2)}|W|/2 and the sufficient condition for linear MIE is S_e^{(2)}>2logμ_{Λ^*}. Family P: two layers of Haar-random (left- and right-unitarily invariant) four-qudit gates acting on square-lattice plaquettes; sites are blocked into 8×4 cells, each cell contains eight four-qudit quartets for the final-layer measurement decomposition, the finite enumeration over τ∈{±1}^8\{(+1,…,+1)} gives a decreasing one-cell factor g_P(q), and q≥88 is the sufficient integer range defined by the condition g_P(q)≤1/μ_{hex}, μ_{hex}=√(2+√2). Family B: four layers of Haar-random (left- and right-unitarily invariant) two-qudit brickwork gates compiled into two plaquette-like layers; each 8×4 cell contains sixteen two-qudit pairs, the finite enumeration over τ∈{±1}^{16}\{(+1,…,+1)} gives a decreasing one-cell factor g_B(q), and q≥134 is the sufficient integer range defined by the condition g_B(q)≤1/μ_{hex}, μ_{hex}=√(2+√2). The enumeration factors g_P(q) and g_B(q) are operationally fixed by summing, for every non-all-positive τ, the product of the local Schatten-2 norm bounds for the untraced one-, two-, or three-qudit reduced states in that cell; for P these bounds are c_1(q)^2=q(q+1)/(q^4+1) and c_2(q)^2=2q^2/(q^4+1), and for B they are c'_1(q)^2=q(q^4+6q^2+1)/(q^2+1)^3 and c'_2(q)=2q/(q^2+1), with additional brickwork split-pair factors bounded by √3/q.

source_span.verbatim: There exist ensembles of unitaries U obtained from natural 2D circuit architectures on q-dimensional qudits of variable depth dC, for which there are values (q,dC)=O(1), such that the average measurement-induced entanglement ... satisfies ... ≥κLx.

hinted_superfamily.definition: The hinted superfamily is the set of the same local architectures at larger depths: depth-d_C four-local plaquette circuits with d_C≥2 and depth-d_C brickwork circuits with d_C≥4. This set contains the proved depth-2 plaquette and depth-4 brickwork subfamilies by set inclusion in d_C, but no monotonicity theorem in d_C is included in Σ_P^{(1)}.

source_span.verbatim: Intuitively, MIE should only increase as a function of dC in the shallow-depth regime... though this argument is not yet rigorous.

robustness_scope.criterion: For every instance in the union of (H) holographic circuits with edge Rényi-2 entropy S_e^{(2)}>2logμ_{Λ^*} and L_y≤L_x^a for a fixed a>0, (P) depth-2 Haar-random four-local plaquette circuits with q∈\mathbb Z and q≥88, and (B) depth-4 Haar-random two-local brickwork circuits with q∈\mathbb Z and q≥134, the proof must give Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}≤L_y exp[-mL_x] for some m>0 after substituting the corresponding local self-avoiding-walk weights into Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}=∑_{W∈\mathrm{SAW}(Λ^*,A,C)}exp[-H(W)]; then F_{\mathrm{SAW}}=-logZ_{\mathrm{SAW}}=Ω(L_x), so Theorem-8-style substitution yields ∑_{s_B}p_{s_B}S(ρ^A_{s_B})≥κL_x for some κ>0 and all sufficiently large L_x.

canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_2=(\mathcal U_{H},\mathsf{SEBD},\mathsf{bMPS},χ,N,S_e^{(2)},Π_2)∈\mathcal O_P^{(2)}, where Π_2 is a proof certificate whose terminal judgement is high-probability failure of polynomial-bond-dimension boundary-MPS representations
canonical_goal.target_object: A proved proposition with endpoint: in the formal square-lattice holographic-circuit regime where the intermediate virtual state has linear half-chain entropy, a column-wise matrix-product-state sampler for random shallow circuits and a column-wise matrix-product-state contraction method for the corresponding random tensor networks cannot keep polynomial bond dimension with bounded error, so the algorithms abort with probability 1-exp[-Ω(√N)].
feasibility_constraints: The lattice is square with √N rows and √N columns, so L_x=√N. The holographic circuit places a bond state |ω_e⟩ on every nearest-neighbour edge, applies independent Haar-random on-site unitaries, with Haar-random meaning distributed according to the left- and right-unitarily invariant probability measure on the on-site unitary group, and measures bulk sites.

The bond entropy threshold is S_e^{(2)}>2.8 bits, where S_e^{(2)}=-log_2 Tr[(Tr_2|ω_e⟩⟨ω_e|)^2]. The number 2.8 is an upper sufficient threshold obtained from S_e^{(2)}>2log_2 μ_{sq}, with μ_{sq} the connective constant of the square lattice and log_2 μ_{sq}<1.4.

The column-wise sampling algorithm \mathsf{SEBD} stores, after measuring previous columns, a one-dimensional virtual conditional state on L_x sites as an MPS and truncates its bond dimension to poly(L_x); it aborts if no poly(L_x)-bond MPS approximation meets the bounded-error criterion.

The column-wise contraction algorithm \mathsf{bMPS} stores the boundary tensor after contracting previous columns as an MPS on L_x legs and truncates its bond dimension to poly(L_x); it aborts if no poly(L_x)-bond MPS approximation meets the bounded-error criterion.

A half-chain entropy lower bound S_{1/2}≥αL_x with α>0 for the stored virtual or boundary state rules out faithful polynomial-bond-dimension representation: an MPS of bond dimension D has half-chain entropy at most logD exactly, and bounded-error approximations to the high-entropy states considered require D=exp[Ω(L_x)].

For tensor-network contraction, the random tensor distribution is p(T)=p_{\mathrm{Gauss}}(T)|||Ψ[T]⟩||^2, where p_{\mathrm{Gauss}} is the density for independent complex-Gaussian tensor entries and |Ψ[T]⟩ is the boundary state obtained by contracting the bulk tensors.

success_set.definition: Σ_P^{(2)}={o_2: Π_2 proves that for square √N×√N random holographic circuits with S_e^{(2)}>2.8 bits, \Pr[\mathsf{SEBD} aborts]≥1-exp[-c√N] for some c>0 and all sufficiently large N; and Π_2 proves that for random tensor networks drawn from p(T)=p_{\mathrm{Gauss}}(T)|||Ψ[T]⟩||^2 with maximally entangled bond dimension χ≥7, \Pr[\mathsf{bMPS} aborts]≥1-exp[-c'√N] for some c'>0 and all sufficiently large N. The integer χ≥7 is fixed operationally by S_e^{(2)}=log_2χ for a maximally entangled bond state and log_2 7>2.8.}

robustness_scope.ambient_space: Pairs (random shallow two-dimensional circuit or random two-dimensional tensor-network ensemble, column-wise MPS boundary algorithm) in which the algorithm represents a one-dimensional virtual or boundary state of length L_x by an MPS whose bond dimension is constrained to be polynomial in L_x.
robustness_scope.indexing_set: {N∈\mathbb N: square √N×√N holographic circuits with S_e^{(2)}>2.8 bits} ∪ {N∈\mathbb N: square √N×√N random tensor networks with p(T)=p_{\mathrm{Gauss}}(T)|||Ψ[T]⟩||^2 and maximally entangled bond dimension χ≥7}

claimed_subfamily.definition: The claimed subfamily is restricted to square-lattice holographic circuits whose bond state has S_e^{(2)}>2.8 bits and to the corresponding square-lattice random tensor-network contraction problem with maximally entangled bond dimension χ≥7. For both tasks, the stored state is tested across a half-chain cut; a self-avoiding-walk free-energy bound gives half-chain entropy Ω(L_x) with probability 1-exp[-Ω(L_x)], and since L_x=√N this becomes an abort probability of 1-exp[-Ω(√N)].

source_span.verbatim: Using the SEBD algorithm to sample from a random holographic circuit on a square √N × √N lattice where the bond state |ωe⟩ has Rényi-2 entanglement entropy Se^(2)>2.8 bits, the probability of the algorithm aborting is 1−e^{−Ω(√N)}. The same holds for using bMPS to contract random tensor networks with bond dimension χ≥7.

hinted_superfamily.definition: The hinted superfamily is the set of architectures for which the intermediate virtual or boundary state produced during a boundary-contraction sampling or tensor-network-contraction sweep has a self-avoiding-walk partition function satisfying Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}≤exp[-αL_x] for some α>0. This set contains the square-lattice holographic and random-tensor-network instances in Σ_P^{(2)}, but no theorem endpoint is required here for every member of the larger set.

source_span.verbatim: More generally, if we look at different circuit architectures, then in regimes where the relevant self-avoiding walk model is ordered... an analogous result will apply.

robustness_scope.criterion: For every square √N×√N holographic-circuit SEBD instance with bond-state Rényi-2 entropy S_e^{(2)}>2.8 bits, and for every corresponding square √N×√N random tensor-network bMPS contraction instance with maximally entangled bond dimension χ≥7 and tensor distribution p(T)=p_{\mathrm{Gauss}}(T)|||Ψ[T]⟩||^2, the proof must show: (i) the stored virtual or boundary state has half-chain entropy at least αL_x with probability at least 1-exp[-βL_x] for constants α,β>0; (ii) every MPS of bond dimension D has half-chain entropy at most logD; and (iii) any polynomial-D boundary algorithm must abort with probability at least 1-exp[-Ω(√N)].

canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_3=(\mathcal U_{Cl},P_U,C_N,Q_U,δ,m,N,Π_3)∈\mathcal O_P^{(3)}, where Π_3 is a proof certificate whose terminal judgement lower-bounds the depth of any classical probabilistic sampler approximating the quantum output distribution
canonical_goal.target_object: A proved proposition with endpoint: for a specified random constant-depth two-dimensional holographic Clifford circuit family, no classical probabilistic circuit of depth o(logN), even with all-to-all connectivity and with the random gates as input, can sample from the quantum output distribution to constant average total-variation accuracy.
feasibility_constraints: The quantum ensemble is the square-lattice holographic Clifford circuit with local qudit dimension q=2^m for an integer m≥6; each site applies an independently sampled four-qudit Clifford unitary U_i; the physical circuit depth is bounded independently of N. A four-qudit Clifford unitary is a unitary that maps every tensor-product generalized Pauli operator on the four q-dimensional qudits to another such Pauli operator under conjugation, up to an overall phase.
For each U, P_U is the exact Born distribution over measurement strings produced by measuring the output quantum state in the specified local basis.

A candidate simulator C_N is a probabilistic classical circuit with unrestricted all-to-all connectivity; it receives the classical descriptions {U_i} as input and outputs a distribution Q_U over the same strings as P_U.
The approximation condition is \mathbb E_{U∼\mathcal U_{Cl}}TV(Q_U,P_U)≤δ, where TV(Q_U,P_U)=\frac12∑_s|Q_U(s)-P_U(s)| and δ>0 is a constant independent of N.
The desired lower bound is depth(C_N)≥c logN for some c>0 independent of N; equivalently, no simulator family with depth(C_N)=o(logN) satisfies the approximation condition.

success_set.definition: Σ_P^{(3)}={o_3: Π_3 proves that there exists a constant δ>0 such that, for every integer m≥6 and every family of probabilistic classical circuits C_N with all-to-all connectivity, if C_N takes {U_i} as input for the q=2^m holographic Clifford ensemble and satisfies \mathbb E_UTV(Q_U,P_U)≤δ, then depth(C_N)=Ω(logN). The numerical threshold m≥6 is operationally fixed by the proof condition (m/2)log2≥log(3μ_{sq}), where μ_{sq} is the square-lattice connective constant; m=6 is included because (6/2)log2≥log(3μ_{sq}), so q=2^m≥64.}

robustness_scope.ambient_space: Pairs (U,C_N) where U is drawn from the claimed random constant-depth holographic Clifford circuit ensemble and C_N is a probabilistic classical circuit attempting to approximate U's output distribution.
robustness_scope.metric_or_divergence: Total variation distance TV(Q_U,P_U)=\frac12∑_s|Q_U(s)-P_U(s)|, averaged over U∼\mathcal U_{Cl}.
robustness_scope.radius_or_budget: A constant δ>0 independent of N satisfying \mathbb E_UTV(Q_U,P_U)≤δ.
robustness_scope.indexing_set: {(m,N,C_N): m∈\mathbb Z, m≥6, N∈\mathbb N, U is a square-lattice holographic Clifford circuit on q=2^m-dimensional qudits, and C_N is any probabilistic classical circuit with all-to-all connectivity}

claimed_subfamily.definition: The claimed subfamily is the random holographic Clifford circuit with q=2^m-dimensional qudits for every integer m≥6, independent four-qudit Clifford gates U_i at each site, and arbitrary all-to-all classical probabilistic simulators constrained only by the average total-variation radius δ. The proof uses a tripartite measurement-induced-entanglement condition: after measuring all but three randomly selected qubits, each one-qubit reduced state has purity below a constant threshold with constant probability, which forces logarithmic classical depth for constant-error sampling.

source_span.verbatim: For some constant δ>0, and for any m≥6, any classical probabilistic circuit that takes {Ui} as input and outputs a distribution that is on average δ-close in total variational distance to the output of the quantum circuit must have depth Ω(log N).

hinted_superfamily.definition: The hinted superfamily is the set of depth-2 four-local circuits at constant q whose post-measurement stabilizer states satisfy the analogous tripartite measurement-induced-entanglement condition used to force logarithmic classical depth. This set is not included in Σ_P^{(3)} because no completed proof certificate for those four-local instances is part of the extracted endpoint.

source_span.verbatim: In principle, we can also combine the arguments that led to Proposition 10 with those that led to Corollary 13 to get a similar result for depth-2 4-local circuits for q=O(1) as well.

robustness_scope.criterion: For every claimed simulator C_N, if \mathbb E_UTV(Q_U,P_U)≤δ for the stated constant δ, then Π_3 must derive depth(C_N)≥c logN for some c>0; hence every depth-o(logN) simulator is outside the success set.

methodological_claim.target_object: A replica-free proof strategy whose endpoint is an entropy lower bound rather than a replica quasientropy estimate: measurement of B followed by outcome-conditioned local operations between A and C is formalised as a one-shot multi-user entanglement-of-assistance protocol for distilling |Φ^{AC}_{d'}⟩=(d')^{-1/2}∑_{j=1}^{d'}|j⟩_A⊗|j⟩_C; the local measurement channel is decomposed into Ising-valued choices σ_i∈{−1,+1}; configurations are grouped by domain walls W separating A from C; Schatten-norm inequalities and 2-design moment identities bound the distillation error by √{d'}Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}f(Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}) with f(x)=(e^x−1)/x; optimizing d' yields ∑_{s_B}p_{s_B}S(ρ^A_{s_B})≥2F_{\mathrm{SAW}}−2log(eF_{\mathrm{SAW}}) for F_{\mathrm{SAW}}≥2.

source_span.verbatim: we develop new replica-free theoretical techniques that leverage tools from multi-user quantum information theory... allowing us to map the problem onto a statistical mechanics model of self-avoiding walks

evidence_channels.formalisation: The methodological claim is the derivation schema |Ψ^{ABC}⟩ ↦ {p_{s_B},|ϕ^{AC}_{s_B}⟩} ↦ error bound \barϵ(d')≤√{d'}Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}(e^{Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}}−1)/Z_{\mathrm{SAW}} ↦ entropy bound E(A:C)≥2F_{\mathrm{SAW}}−2log(eF_{\mathrm{SAW}}), where F_{\mathrm{SAW}}=-logZ_{\mathrm{SAW}}; no analytic continuation in a replica index α is part of this derivation.

source_span.verbatim: We analyse the entanglement structure of states generated by random constant-depth two-dimensional quantum circuits... First, we show that standard algorithms based on matrix product states ... will fail... In addition, we also prove that these random constant-depth quantum circuits cannot be simulated by any classical circuit of sublogarithmic depth.

stated_goal.formalisation: The stated goal is an instrumental conjunction of three end-state propositions: first, for local measurements on region B of a state prepared by a random constant-depth two-dimensional quantum circuit or random holographic tensor network, prove a lower bound on the average post-measurement entropy ∑_{s_B}p_{s_B}S(ρ^A_{s_B}) and instantiate it as an extensive inequality \mathbb E_U∑_{s_B}p_{s_B}S(ρ^A_{s_B})≥κL_x with κ>0; second, use the resulting linear entanglement of the one-dimensional boundary state encountered by matrix-product-state boundary methods to prove that SEBD sampling and bMPS tensor-network contraction abort with probability 1−exp[−Ω(√N)] in the stated regimes; third, prove that for a constant-depth holographic Clifford circuit on q=2^m-dimensional qudits with m≥6, every probabilistic classical circuit whose output distribution is on average within a fixed total-variation distance δ of the quantum output distribution has depth Ω(logN).

source_span.paragraph_or_line: Definitions of MIE; Theorem 8; Corollaries 9, 12, 13; Propositions 10, 11
source_span.verbatim: Theorem 8 gives us a general bound on measurement-induced entanglement... we can now apply this result to specific families of random quantum circuits.

operational_goal.formalisation: The operational goal is the proof pipeline: define the post-measurement ensemble by p_{s_B}=⟨s_B|ρ^B|s_B⟩ and |ϕ^{AC}_{s_B}⟩=p_{s_B}^{-1/2}(⟨s_B|⊗I_{AC})|Ψ^{ABC}⟩; define E(A:C)=∑_{s_B}p_{s_B}S(Tr_C|ϕ^{AC}_{s_B}⟩⟨ϕ^{AC}_{s_B}|); prove E(A:C)≥2F_{\mathrm{SAW}}−2log(eF_{\mathrm{SAW}}) when F_{\mathrm{SAW}}=-log∑_{W}exp[-H(W)]≥2; prove F_{\mathrm{SAW}}=Ω(L_x) for holographic, depth-2 four-local, and depth-4 brickwork random ensembles; translate Ω(L_x) virtual or boundary entanglement into failure of polynomial-bond-dimension MPS boundary algorithms; and prove the Clifford-circuit Ω(logN) classical-depth lower bound under average total-variation error.

inference_basis: The abstract and overview name three end-state claims: macroscopic long-ranged MIE, MPS/bMPS failure, and sublogarithmic classical-depth nonsimulability.
The formal centre of the paper is Theorem 8, whose output variable is E(A:C) and whose success predicate is an entropy lower bound expressed through F_{SAW}.
Corollary 9 and Propositions 10/11 instantiate G1 for holographic, four-local plaquette, and brickwork random ensembles at constant q and constant depth.
Section VI.D uses the G1 high-MIE condition to derive G2, so G2 is instrumental downstream of G1 rather than independent.
Section VI.E and Appendix F adapt the MIE machinery to tripartite stabilizer entanglement to derive G3, so G3 is a distinct downstream complexity-theoretic goal.

The replica-free entanglement-of-assistance/self-avoiding-walk construction is repeatedly framed as how the result is obtained and is therefore represented as methodological_claim rather than as another canonical end-state goal.
implicit_goal.formalisation: The maximal-fit implicit structure is an instrumental chain: the primary endpoint is a reusable high-measurement-induced-entanglement entropy theorem for ∑_{s_B}p_{s_B}S(ρ^A_{s_B}); a downstream algorithmic endpoint uses the same high-entanglement condition to prove average-case failure of polynomial-bond-dimension matrix-product-state boundary algorithms; a distinct downstream complexity-theoretic endpoint uses an analogous tripartite stabilizer-entanglement condition to prove Ω(logN) depth for classical probabilistic simulation. The replica-free entanglement-of-assistance and self-avoiding-walk machinery is a derivation method rather than a separate desired end-state.

excluded_aims.verbatim: Quantum entanglement is a vital resource that can be utilised to achieve tasks that would not be possible in a classical world, such as unconditionally secure cryptography and high-precision sensing.

paper_goal.consistency_relation_derivation: The formal stated and operational goals align on three instrumental end-state propositions: a rigorous average-MIE lower bound plus constant-depth extensive-MIE instantiations, MPS/bMPS boundary-algorithm failure, and an Ω(logN) classical-depth lower bound. The relation is framing_divergence rather than aligned because the stated framing also contains methodological content—replica-free multi-user quantum-information techniques and a self-avoiding-walk mapping—and broad quantum-advantage motivation; those elements are encoded as methodological_claim or excluded_aims rather than as additional canonical end-state goals.
